tasks.short: Design or develop automated testing tools.

steps.what: Design what the automated testing tools must do.
Develop the tool inside that design.
Draft a small check of the tool's own behaviour.

loop.input: the behaviours named in the design note
loop.output: a check list that names only those behaviours
loop.check: every check cites a behaviour from the note; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; an unnamed behaviour is not added
loop.why_not_simpler: whether the tool is fit to use is the decision

steps.what: Decide if the automated tool is fit to use.
Store the tool and the design note.

tasks.design: The tester designs what the tool must do, then develops it. A check list may name only behaviours in that design. The tester decides the tool is fit. Storage follows. The tool is not generated from a wish.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tools grew as scripts nobody else could run, with no statement of what they guaranteed.
tasks.enabler_now: A named behaviour can become a check. Designing the tool cannot.
tasks.still_hard: What the tool should refuse to hide, and how it should fail, stay a design judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows which check would make a green run meaningless.
tasks.altitude: The check list takes less rewriting. Design and development stay with the tester.

reach.task: Run the stored tool on a change
reach.learn: What the tool is allowed to claim

evidence.claim: A check that cites a designed behaviour can be stored. The design of a testing tool cannot be generated.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester designs and develops the tool. Updating an existing script is a different task. Buying a tool is a different task.
Structured input: behaviour name, input, expected result, from the design note. Producer is the tester. A check citing an unnamed behaviour is discarded.
Development time stays. The tool is stored only after the fit decision.
unknowns: Where do internal tools live today?
Who else may rely on a tool's result?
research_questions: How many tools exist that only one person can run?

already_counted.description: Developing the tool is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire tools the tester has withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: fit decision the tester made for that tool

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the design note is vague, the check list is empty and the development stays. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Install recreations of production environments for testing.

steps.what: Install recreations of the production environments.
Configure each recreation to match production.
List the software versions the recreation must match.
Run a short performance check before testing.

tasks.design: Installing and configuring a recreation of production stays the tester's work on {OPS_SYSTEM}. A list of software versions shows what production is running. A short performance check happens before the recreation is used. The install is not treated as a script that always works.
tasks.previous_blocker: Environments were built from memory, and a test passed on a machine unlike production.
tasks.enabler_now: A version list is a query. Making the recreation match is hands-on.
tasks.still_hard: A setting that production never wrote down, and hardware the lab does not have, stay hard.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows which difference would make the test lie.
tasks.altitude: The version list is no longer copied by hand. Install, configure and the check stay.

reach.task: Know which production versions the recreation matches

evidence.claim: Listing installed versions is a query. Recreating a production environment is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester installs and configures the recreation. Running the full test is a different task. Changing production is not allowed from here.
Structured input: environment name, software name, version. Producer is the production inventory. A version the inventory does not have is shown as unknown.
Install and configure time stay. The lab is not production, and the check says so.
unknowns: Is there an inventory of production versions?
research_questions: How often does a test pass only because the lab differed?

already_counted.description: Installing the recreation is already the remaining time on that step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If production versions are unknown, the list is empty and the install stays a manual match. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work with field staff or customers to diagnose problems.

steps.what: Collaborate with field staff or customers.
Evaluate and diagnose the problems with them.
Recommend possible solutions, or recommend none.
File the recommendation that was agreed.

tasks.design: The collaboration, the diagnosis and the recommendation stay a conversation with field staff or the customer. The file is a record of what was agreed, not a diagnosis produced apart from them. No recommendation is sent that the tester did not say.
tasks.previous_blocker: The call had no record, so the next person repeated the same questions.
tasks.enabler_now: A record can hold the recommendation the tester already made. It cannot hold the call.
tasks.still_hard: A problem that only appears on their site, with their data, stays a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The tester hears the workaround they already use, which a ticket does not say.
tasks.altitude: The recommendation has a record. The call, the diagnosis and the advice stay.

reach.task: Try only the recommendation that was agreed
reach.learn: What was ruled out on the call

evidence.claim: Filing an agreed recommendation is a record. Diagnosing with a customer is not.
A customer call can include personal data. The record should keep the problem and the recommendation, not a copy of their private files.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester collaborates, diagnoses and recommends. A later code fix is the developer. Support may own the relationship.
Structured input: ticket id, recommendation text the tester confirms. Producer is the tester after the call. An empty recommendation is filed as none.
Call time stays. The record is not a second conversation.
unknowns: May the tester talk to the customer directly?
What from the call may be stored?
research_questions: How often is the same customer problem reopened with no record?

already_counted.description: The call with the customer is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire records after the problem is closed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the customer will not join a call, there is nothing to file and the diagnosis does not happen. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Agree the scope with the user or the third party.
Coordinate the testing window and the build.
Run the testing the third party owns.
Accept the third-party result or send it back.

tasks.design: The tester agrees the scope and coordinates the window and the build. The user or third party runs their own testing. The tester accepts the result or sends it back. Their hours are not counted as the tester's saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Third-party testing was a date in a mail, and the build they used was unclear.
tasks.enabler_now: A window and a build id can be shared. Accepting their result is a review.
tasks.still_hard: A result the tester cannot replay, because the party will not share the steps, stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows when a passed result did not cover the agreed scope.
tasks.altitude: The window and the build are visible. Agreeing scope, coordinating and accepting the result stay.

reach.task: Run only the agreed scope on the named build

evidence.claim: Sharing a build id and a window is coordination. Accepting a third party's result is not automatic.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester coordinates and accepts. The third party performs the testing. Visiting a beta site is a different task.
Structured input: party, scope ids, build id, window. Producer is the tester after agreement. A result with no build id is not accepted.
The party's time stays theirs. Acceptance is remaining tester time.
unknowns: Who may accept a third-party result?
research_questions: How often is the wrong build given to the party?

already_counted.description: Accepting the result is already the remaining time on that step.
The party's own testing is already remaining time on their step.

incremental.description: Close windows after the build is withdrawn.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the party will not name a build, acceptance stays a conversation and little else changes. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Designing a tool, installing a production-like environment, and talking to a customer stay the tester's. A third party runs their own testing. The tester accepts or returns the result.
reach: A developer can run a tool that has a design note.
A third party gets one build and one window.
skills_to_grow: Do not store a tool that has no stated behaviour.
Send back a result that misses the agreed scope.
role.ambitious_version: A customer recommendation is a record of what was said, and a third-party result names the build.

job.title: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers
